Russians are visa-free for stays of up to 45 days (this exemption is currently valid until 2028-03-05, per a March 2025 announcement extending it). Your passport just needs to be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date.

If you need to stay longer than 45 days, Russians can also get an e-Visa: up to 90 days, USD 25 (single entry) or USD 50 (multiple entry), processed in 2-3 business days, and usable at any of the approved air/land/sea ports (not restricted to one nominated port). Apply at evisa.gov.vn.

This data is current as of 2026-08-17 — I'd recommend double-checking at evisa.gov.vn before you travel, since policy can change.

Yes — Brits (UK passport holders) can visit Vietnam visa-free. You can stay up to 45 days without a visa, under a unilateral exemption that's currently extended through 2028-03-05.

Key details:
- Max stay: 45 days per visit, no visa needed
- Your passport must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date
- This exemption is set to expire 2028-03-05, so it's worth checking closer to your travel date that it hasn't changed

If you ever want to stay longer than 45 days, an e-Visa is available to all nationalities (including the UK) for up to 90 days, costing USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), applied for at evisa.gov.vn.

Data as of 2026-08-17 — I'd recommend double-checking current policy at evisa.gov.vn before you travel, just in case anything's changed.

2. **Key details:**
   - e-Visa covers stays up to 90 days, so a 30-day trip is well within range.
   - Cost: USD 25 (single entry) or USD 50 (multiple entry).
   - Processing: 2-3 business days (faster/expedited options may be available at extra cost).
   - Valid for entry by air, land, or sea, at any of the approved ports (83 listed in this dataset) — you're not restricted to a single nominated port, but verify the current port list at evisa.gov.vn before you travel.

3. **How to apply:** https://evisa.gov.vn/

4. **Data caveat:** This is based on policy data as of 2026-08-17. Always double-check current requirements at evisa.gov.vn before you travel, since visa-free allowances and e-Visa terms can change.

Good news on the basic entry rule: as a Polish citizen you're visa-free for stays up to 45 days (Resolution 229/NQ-CP), which comfortably covers a one-week trip, and this exemption is currently valid through 2028-08-14. No visa or e-Visa fee is needed for entry itself.

One important catch, though: the dataset's own record of this exemption specifies it's granted for "tourism purpose." Your trip is a week of business meetings, not tourism, so it's worth confirming before you fly whether business meetings fall within the visa-free allowance or whether Vietnam expects business travelers to hold an e-Visa or business visa instead. Immigration authorities can be strict about purpose-of-visit mismatches at the border.

To be safe, you have a low-cost fallback either way: Vietnam's e-Visa is open to all nationalities (including Poland), allows stays up to 90 days, costs USD 25 (single-entry) or 50 (multiple-entry), takes about 2-3 business days to process, and can be used at any of the approved entry ports (air, land, or sea) — it's not restricted to one nominated port. Applying for one explicitly as a business e-Visa would remove any ambiguity about purpose of travel.

A couple of housekeeping items regardless of route: your passport needs at least 180 days' validity remaining from your entry date, and this data is current as of 2026-08-17 — I'd recommend double-checking the tourism-vs-business condition and current rules directly at evisa.gov.vn before you travel, since a business-purpose mismatch is the kind of detail that can cause problems at immigration even when the visa-free duration itself is generous.

As a Belarusian citizen you fall under the Vietnam-Belarus bilateral visa exemption (effective 30 Jan 2025): visa-free entry for up to 30 days per entry, BUT total visa-free days in a calendar year can't exceed 90.

You've already used 70 of those 90 days in 2026, so only 20 visa-free days remain this year — not the 30 you're planning. A 30-day trip now would put you at 100 days for the year, 10 days over the cap.

Your options:
1. Shorten the trip to 20 days (or less) to stay within the 90-day annual visa-free allowance.
2. Apply for an e-Visa instead for the full 30 days. It's open to all nationalities, costs USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), takes about 2-3 business days to process, and lets you enter by air, land, or sea through any of 83 approved ports (up to 90 days per stay). The e-Visa is a separate authorization from the bilateral visa-free scheme, so it isn't limited by that 90-day annual visa-free count.

Also: your passport must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date.

Data as of 2026-08-17 — please verify the current policy at evisa.gov.vn before booking, since bilateral exemption terms can change.

- **What you actually need**: Since you want 120 days, you'll need to apply for an embassy/consulate visa in the appropriate category (e.g. LV visitor/work visa, DT investment visa, or GD education visa, depending on your purpose of travel) through a Vietnamese embassy or consulate rather than the online e-Visa portal.
- Make sure your passport is valid for at least 180 days from your entry date.
